text:
maria: quick heads-up — product wants a dashboard that can click from a high P90 route latency down to the originating request trace (request_id/trace_id) for debugging. we need infra + runtime input on how to wire IDs through metrics/logs without exploding cardinality or cost

sam: agree we can do this but we should be explicit about what "click-to-trace" means. options: emit trace_id as a log field and provide links from metrics to the logs, or emit trace_id as a metric label (dangerous for cardinality). my recommendation: logs + an indexed lookup service + dashboards that surface a small sample of trace_ids per bucket. :thinking_face:

kevin: from console/UX POV we want a single click on a latency bar -> open trace view in the APM. latency buckets should show 3 sample traces each. we need the runtime to guarantee propagation of a stable request_id header and to attach trace_id to the generated spans. also need a standard field name (eg X-Request-Id / X-Redwood-Req).

liz: SRE concern: if we start attaching request_id to metrics (counters/histograms) we'll create high-cardinality metrics and blow up Prometheus. can't do that. logs + traces is fine but dashboards need a deterministic way to jump to the trace. we already index logs by request_id in our ELK for 30d — we could reuse that index if runtime populates header.

anita: infra note: our metrics ingest (metering pipeline) currently strips unknown labels at ingest. adding a trace_id label to the time series will be rejected anyway. if the plan is to add labels, we need a new path that stores request-linked events in the trace store or a separate low-ttl metrics table. both are extra infra work + cost.

maria: ok so consensus: do NOT add request_id as a prometheus-style label. instead: (1) runtime must propagate X-Redwood-Req unless client provides X-Request-Id, (2) runtime should attach trace_id/span_id to trace export and to structured logs, (3) dashboards should resolve via logs or trace-store lookup. sound right?

sam: yep. implementation details: in the serving runtime we can 1) accept incoming X-Request-Id or generate one at the edge, 2) set Context.TraceID in our tracing lib, 3) ensure exporters include span.trace_id as field, 4) include a minimal per-request metadata event to the telemetry pipeline containing {trace_id, route, bucket, sampling_level} (this is small and not stored in prometheus, rather in a short-retention lookup table). example config snippet: ```yaml
# runtime config (pseudocode)
headers:
  accept_request_id: ["X-Request-Id","X-Redwood-Req"]
generate_if_missing: true
trace:
  inject_header: "X-Redwood-Trace"
  export_fields: ["trace_id","span_id","service","route"]
telemetry_lookup_ttl: 72h
```

kevin: dashboards should call an internal lookup API to translate a selected bucket -> sample trace_ids. that API can read from the telemetry lookup table. we can limit to 3 samples per bucket to keep UI fast. UI needs a config option to enable/disable sample linking (enterprise customers might want it off).

liz: sampling policy — we need to be careful. don't send full traces for every request. propose: default adaptive sampling: always keep all errors and high-latency tails, plus a small uniform sample (0.5% or tuneable). we can also add a rate cap per route. document will need SLA/cost estimates.

anita: for infra: building telemetry lookup store: small key-value DB keyed by trace_id -> metadata (route, timestamp, cost_flag). retention default 72h as sam suggested. storage is tiny if we only store one small row per traced request and we only trace sampled requests. estimate: at 1k RPS * 0.5% sample * 72h -> ~3M rows, ~ ~300MB/day compressed. acceptable. we also need an auth gateway so dashboards can't abuse the lookup API.

maria: nice. open question: how do we link dashboard signals (histogram buckets) to trace samples deterministically? we should pick a bucketing algorithm and define which sample keys are eligible. maybe collect per-request a bucket id computed by route + latency_bucket and store that in the lookup row.

sam: yep. runtime will compute bucket = route + latency_bucket(p50/p90/p99) at response time and write telemetry_lookup row: {trace_id, route, bucket, duration_ms, status_code, sample_tag}. Dashboard will query endpoint /lookup?route=X&bucket=Y and get N trace_ids (with metadata + URL to open in APM). pseudo-response: ```json
[{"trace_id":"abc123","duration_ms":1200,"ts":1784120000,"trace_url":"https://apm/trace/abc123"}, ...]
```

dave: small infra ask: add an audit log for who requests trace lookups in the console (privacy/compliance). also need redaction rules. some customers will want to scrub PII before storing lookup rows if request payloads can contain PII. store only route/timestamp/status/duration/ids — no user payloads.

kevin: UX follow-up: console will show a "Show sample traces" toggle and a sampling badge that indicates "showing sampled traces (0.5%)". if there are no samples for a bucket, UI should show a message and suggest increasing sample rate for that route.

maria: action items: sam -> proto runtime PR to add header propagation + telemetry lookup event (ETA 2w). anita -> infra design doc for lookup store + auth + retention + cost estimate (ETA 1w). kevin -> console mockups + lookup API contract (ETA 1w). liz -> run risk/privacy checklist and recommend redaction rules (ETA 1w). i'll draft the product acceptance criteria.

sam: I'll also include a togglable env var to disable lookup emission per-deployment for customers on Dedicated/Private.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-lookup-service v0.1 -> staging (sha: ab12c3) :rocket:

maria: thanks all. will sync after the infra doc lands. please add any follow-ups inline. :thumbsup:
